claim: Enemy intelligence budget: NSMART is the CURRENT number of promoted (attacking/smart) enemies — the debit side of the budget. Promotions raise it, deaths of smart enemies lower it; it must reach zero at wave end (the IFN DEBUG oracle).

source.verbatim: NSMART	RMB	1	CURRENT NUMBER OF ATTACKING ENEMIES

claim: Enemy intelligence budget: WSMART is the WANTED number of smart enemies for the wave — the target the budget grows toward. Seeded from the wave pursuit nibble and bumped every 15 s while enemies live. A dumb enemy promotes while NSMART < WSMART.

source.verbatim: WSMART	RMB	1	NUMBER OF ENEMIES THAT SHOULD ATTACK IN A WAVE

claim: PCHASE is the per-enemy smart flag: 1 = promoted/chasing (running a smart brain), 0 = dumb (running LINET). Promotion sets it 1; a death debits NSMART by exactly this flag, so a dumb death credits nothing and a smart death credits one.

source.verbatim: PCHASE	RMB	1		ENEMIES CHASE (=1) OR NON-CHASE (=0) FLAG

claim: EMYTIM is the PAUSE TIME BETWEEN ENEMIES MOVEMENTS — an integrate-every-Nth-frame DIVIDER (the enemy process naps EMYTIM frames between steps), NOT a per-step speed scale. 2 on waves 1-2 slows enemies to half rate; 1 otherwise.

source.verbatim: EMYTIM	RMB	1	PAUSE TIME BETWEEN ENEMIES MOVEMENTS

claim: WSMART is seeded from the wave pursuit NIBBLE: the low four bits of WPERSUE (ANDA #$0F) become the wanted-smart count. This is the budget INPUT jt2-5 (wave machine) will supply; jt2-2 stubs it as a parameter.
The masked pursuit nibble is stored to WSMART — the per-wave seed of the intelligence budget target (WBEGIN, JOUSTRV4.SRC:2072-2077).

Intelligence growth cadence: PDELAY reloads to 112 and the comment states the interval outright — AFTER 15 SECONDS BUMP NBR OF INTELLIGENT PEOPLE. Combined with the 8-frame nap (EMYOK PCNAP 8) this is 112x8 = 896 frames ~= 15 s at ~60 Hz.

source.verbatim: EMY2	LDA	#112		AFTER 15 SECONDS BUMP NBR OF INTELLIGENT PEOPLE

claim: The growth timer naps 8 frames per decrement (EMYOK PCNAP 8): the 112-count PDELAY is decremented once every 8 frames while enemies live, so a WSMART bump lands every 112x8 = 896 frames.
When the 15-second timer expires while enemies live, WSMART is bumped by one (INC WSMART) — the intelligence budget grows, allowing one more promotion.
The WSMART growth saturates at 255: INC WSMART / BNE EMY2 / DEC WSMART restores the value if the increment wrapped to zero, so the target never rolls over.

Promotion debits the budget: the dumb LINET brain, on finding NSMART < WSMART, jumps here and does INC NSMART (JUST GOT SMARTER) — one more attacking enemy, consuming one unit of the WSMART allowance.

source.verbatim: LNTSMT	INC	NSMART		JUST GOT SMARTER

claim: Promotion invariant (IFN DEBUG oracle): before promoting, PCHASE had BETTER BE ZERO — an already-smart enemy is never re-promoted. This is the no-double-promote bookkeeping oracle for the budget tests.

source.verbatim: LDA	PCHASE,U	DEBUG, BETTER BE ZERO

claim: The promotion target is data: PDECSN,U points at the enemy decision block that carries which smart brain this enemy becomes (bounder/hunter/shadow-lord).

DSMART,X (within the PDECSN decision block) is the address of the smart brain to run on promotion — BOUNDR, B2UNDR, or SHADOW; it is stored to PJOY and jumped to, so the promoted enemy immediately runs its smart brain.
Second promotion path: a buzzard remounted by its thrown rider also promotes (MOUNRI INC NSMART, JUST GOT SMARTER), debiting the budget the same way LINET promotion does.

source.verbatim: MOUNRI	INC	NSMART		JUST GOT SMARTER

claim: Death credits the budget back: on an enemy death, NSMART is reduced (BUMP DOWN SMARTNESS VARIABLE) by that enemy PCHASE flag.

source.verbatim: LDA	NSMART		BUMP DOWN SMARTNESS VARIABLE

claim: The death credit equals the PCHASE flag (SUBA PCHASE,U): a smart enemy (PCHASE=1) credits one back to NSMART, a dumb enemy (PCHASE=0) credits nothing — the exact inverse of promotion.
Each enemy death also decrements NENEMY, the number of enemies on the screen — the count that must reach zero (with NSMART) at wave end.

source.verbatim: DEC	NENEMY		DECREMENT NBR OF ENEMIES ON THE SCREEN

claim: Budget bookkeeping oracle (IFN DEBUG): at wave normalise (WNRM) with all enemies dead, NSMART THIS HAD BETTER BE ZERO — the promotions/deaths ledger balances to zero. jt2-2 uses this as a test oracle.

source.verbatim: LDA	NSMART		THIS HAD BETTER BE ZERO!!!!!!!!!!

claim: Companion oracle: NENEMY THIS HAD BETTER BE ZERO at wave normalise — no enemy processes survive into the next wave.

source.verbatim: 41$	LDA	NENEMY		THIS HAD BETTER BE ZERO!!!!!!!!!!

claim: EMYTIM resets to 1 at wave normalise (NO ENEMY SLOW DOWN) — the default divider is every-frame; the halved rate is only set for waves 1-2.
The slow-down divider value is literally 2 (LDA #2 -> STA EMYTIM), set when TBRIDGE marks the 1st/2nd wave — enemies integrate every 2nd frame.

EMYTIM is consumed as a process NAP count (LDA EMYTIM / JSR VNAPTPC): the enemy/egg process sleeps EMYTIM frames between integration steps, which is what makes it a DIVIDER — half the steps over any window when EMYTIM=2, not a scaled velocity.
VNAPTPC naps the process for the accumulator frame count then resumes (NAPTPC, SYSTEM.SRC:222) — the mechanism by which EMYTIM divides the enemy update rate onto the jt2-1 frame-nap scheduler.
The hunter (advanced bounder, B2UNDR) has a horizontal look-ahead length B2XLEN = 27+4 = 31 that the plain bounder lacks: it projects its path and slows/turns before flying into a cliff (B2DIR).
The shadow lord also carries a horizontal look-ahead length SHXLEN = 27+4 = 31 (SHDIR), the cliff-avoidance the plain bounder does not perform.

Shadow-lord descent is distinct: SHDN sets NO FLAPING WINGS (CLRB, wings up) and free-falls toward the target, only flapping to escape the lava below cliff5 — where the bounder/hunter actively brake their descent at a Y-velocity threshold.
Shadow-lord level flight tracks the PLAYER line directly (SHLEP: LDB PPOSY+1,X PLAYERS LINE TO TRACK) — it hunts the player altitude, distinguishing it from bounder/hunter.

source.verbatim: LDB	PPOSY+1,X	PLAYERS LINE TO TRACK

claim: By contrast the bounder level flight remembers its OWN line to track (BOLEV: LDD PPOSY,U REMEMBER LINE TO TRACK), not the players — the cited difference behind AC-4 pursuit distinctions.

source.verbatim: LDD	PPOSY,U		REMEMBER LINE TO TRACK
